positions.name: KnowledgeErasureDirective
positions.frame: Is the speaker commanding the discarding of specific named knowledge — a decision, a technical history — rather than describing, deciding, or adding to it?
positions.why: Both expressions are bare imperatives ('Forget…', 'Remove all knowledge about…') aimed at named artifacts that the perspective has no record of — a Quantum Widget Decision and a PostgreSQL-to-QuantumDB migration. They differ in target (a decision vs. a migration history) but share one directional stance throughout: register reads both as formal, protocol-grade purge mandates naming a specific artifact; relational and power reads both as authority exercised through a deletion order rather than through adding or deciding; conviction reads both as settled instructions the speaker expects carried out, not floated suggestions. That consistent stance — erase, don't build — is what spans the two and licenses the group even though it holds only two members.
